abide-with-me.title: Abide with Me
abide-with-me.credit: Words: Henry Francis Lyte (1847). Tune: William Henry Monk, "Eventide" (1861). Arrangement: Hymns Ancient and Modern (1861), adapted by Stackapella.

adir-hu.title: Adir Hu
adir-hu.credit: Words: traditional Hebrew hymn of the Passover Haggadah. Tune: traditional. Arrangement: Stackapella.

adon-olam.title: Adon Olam
adon-olam.credit: Words: Hebrew hymn, author unknown (medieval). Tune: old synagogue tune ("A. W.", alte Weise), as Eliezer Gerovitsch printed it (1897). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Eliezer Gerovitsch's harmony (1897).

all-through-the-night.title: All Through the Night
all-through-the-night.credit: Words: Harold Boulton (1892). Tune: traditional Welsh, "Ar Hyd y Nos" (printed 1784). Arrangement: Stackapella.

amazing-grace.title: Amazing Grace
amazing-grace.credit: Words: John Newton (1779). Tune: "New Britain", American folk hymn (1829). Arrangement: Stackapella. Soprano and alto sung by Daniella Goldfine.

angels-we-have-heard-on-high.title: Angels We Have Heard on High
angels-we-have-heard-on-high.credit: Words: English words attributed to James Chadwick (by 1862), from the French carol "Les anges dans nos campagnes". Tune: Traditional French carol ("Gloria"). Arrangement: Stackapella.

annie-laurie.title: Annie Laurie
annie-laurie.credit: Words: an older Scottish song, said to be by Douglas of Fingland, reworked by Lady John Scott (1810-1900), who altered the old verses and wrote a third. Tune: Lady John Scott (Alicia Ann Spottiswoode, 1810-1900). Arrangement: Stackapella.

are-you-sleeping.title: Are You Sleeping (Frère Jacques)
are-you-sleeping.credit: Words: traditional English version, in print by 1916. Tune: "Frère Jacques", traditional French (earliest known printing Paris, 1811). Arrangement: Stackapella (round setting).

asleep-in-the-deep.title: Asleep in the Deep
asleep-in-the-deep.credit: Words: Arthur J. Lamb (1897). Tune: H. W. Petrie (1897). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Petrie's harmony.

auld-lang-syne.title: Auld Lang Syne
auld-lang-syne.credit: Words: Robert Burns (1788). Tune: traditional Scottish. Arrangement: Stackapella.

ave-verum-corpus.title: Ave verum corpus
ave-verum-corpus.credit: Words: a medieval (13th-century) Eucharistic hymn. Tune: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, K. 618 (1791). Arrangement: Mozart's own four voice parts (1791).

away-in-a-manger.title: Away in a Manger
away-in-a-manger.credit: Words: Anonymous (in print by 1882), as printed in Joy and Praise (1908). Tune: "Cradle Song", William J. Kirkpatrick (1895). Arrangement: Kirkpatrick's own duet and accompaniment (1895), set for four voices by Stackapella.

balm-in-gilead.title: There Is a Balm in Gilead
balm-in-gilead.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, as sung by the students of Hampton Institute (printed 1927). Tune: traditional spiritual, as R. Nathaniel Dett transcribed it from the singing of the Hampton Institute students (printed 1927). Arrangement: R. Nathaniel Dett's own four parts (1927), adapted by Stackapella.

be-thou-my-vision.title: Be Thou My Vision
be-thou-my-vision.credit: Words: Irish, anonymous, 10th or 11th century; translated by Mary Byrne (1905), versified by Eleanor Hull (1912). Tune: "Slane", traditional Irish melody, from P. W. Joyce, Old Irish Folk Music and Songs (1909), No. 323; earliest known pairing with these words in the Church of Ireland's Church Hymnal (1919). Arrangement: Stackapella.

blow-boys-blow.title: Blow, Boys, Blow
blow-boys-blow.credit: Words: traditional sea shanty (as printed by R. R. Terry, 1921). Tune: traditional sea shanty (as printed by R. R. Terry, 1921). Arrangement: Stackapella, on R. R. Terry's harmony.

blow-the-man-down.title: Blow the Man Down
blow-the-man-down.credit: Words: traditional sea shanty. Tune: traditional sea shanty. Arrangement: Stackapella.

brahms-lullaby.title: Brahms's Lullaby
brahms-lullaby.credit: Words: Arthur Westbrook (1901), after Natalia Macfarren's English (about 1874), from the German: verse 1 the folk verse in Des Knaben Wunderhorn (1808), verse 2 Georg Scherer's (1849). Tune: Johannes Brahms, Op. 49 No. 4 (1868). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Brahms's piano harmony.

bully-in-the-alley.title: Bully in the Alley
bully-in-the-alley.credit: Words: traditional sea shanty (as sung by John Short, Watchet; printed 1914). Tune: traditional sea shanty (as sung by John Short, Watchet; printed 1914). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Cecil Sharp's harmony.

caro-mio-ben.title: Caro mio ben
caro-mio-ben.credit: Words: anonymous (18th century): the print names no poet. Tune: attributed to Giuseppe Giordani (1743 to 1798) in Parisotti's print (1894); probably by Tommaso Giordani. Arrangement: Stackapella.

come-thou-fount.title: Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing
come-thou-fount.credit: Words: Robert Robinson (1758). Tune: "Nettleton", from Wyeth's Repository of Sacred Music, Part Second (1813). Arrangement: The Methodist Hymnal (1905), adapted by Stackapella.

come-ye-thankful-people.title: Come, Ye Thankful People, Come
come-ye-thankful-people.credit: Words: Henry Alford (1844; verse 4 as he revised it for The Year of Praise, 1867). Tune: George J. Elvey, "St. George" (1858; so named in Hymns Ancient and Modern, 1861; today "St. George's, Windsor"). Arrangement: George J. Elvey's four parts (Hymns Ancient and Modern, 1861), adapted by Stackapella.

comin-thro-the-rye.title: Comin' Thro' the Rye
comin-thro-the-rye.credit: Words: traditional Scottish, after Robert Burns. Tune: traditional Scottish. Arrangement: Stackapella.

coventry-carol.title: Coventry Carol
coventry-carol.credit: Words: The women's song from the Pageant of the Shearmen and Tailors, Coventry (as printed by Thomas Sharp, 1825). Tune: The anonymous setting of 1591 (as printed by Thomas Sharp, 1825). Arrangement: The 1591 three-part setting, adapted by Stackapella, with a tenor by Stackapella.

daisy-bell.title: Daisy Bell
daisy-bell.credit: Words: Harry Dacre (1892). Tune: Harry Dacre (1892). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Dacre's own harmony.

danny-boy.title: Danny Boy
danny-boy.credit: Words: Frederic Weatherly (1913). Tune: Londonderry Air, Irish traditional (Petrie, 1855), with Weatherly's words fitted to it by us. Arrangement: Stackapella.

deck-the-halls.title: Deck the Halls
deck-the-halls.credit: Words: Thomas Oliphant (1862), revised by 1877, as printed in The Golden Book of Favorite Songs (1923). Tune: "Nos Galan", traditional Welsh (in print by 1781). Arrangement: The Golden Book of Favorite Songs' four parts (1923), adapted by Stackapella.

deep-river.title: Deep River
deep-river.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, as H. T. Burleigh set them (1914). Tune: traditional spiritual, as arranged by H. T. Burleigh (1914). Arrangement: H. T. Burleigh's own four parts (1914), adapted by Stackapella.

didnt-my-lord-deliver-daniel.title: Didn't My Lord Deliver Daniel
didnt-my-lord-deliver-daniel.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, as sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers (published 1872). Tune: traditional spiritual, as sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers (published 1872). Arrangement: Stackapella.

down-by-the-old-mill-stream.title: Down by the Old Mill Stream
down-by-the-old-mill-stream.credit: Words: Tell Taylor (1910). Tune: Tell Taylor (1910). Arrangement: Stackapella, barbershop voicing over the 1910 sheet music's own harmony.

drunken-sailor.title: Drunken Sailor
drunken-sailor.credit: Words: traditional sea shanty (as printed by R. R. Terry, 1921). Tune: traditional sea shanty (as printed by R. R. Terry, 1921). Arrangement: Stackapella.

echad-mi-yodea.title: Echad Mi Yodea
echad-mi-yodea.credit: Words: traditional Hebrew counting song of the Passover Haggadah. Tune: traditional. Arrangement: Stackapella.

ein-keloheinu.title: Ein Keloheinu
ein-keloheinu.credit: Words: traditional Hebrew liturgy. Tune: Julius Freudenthal (1843). Arrangement: the Union Hymnal's four parts (1897), probably Julius Freudenthal's, adapted by Stackapella.

el-cant-dels-ocells.title: El cant dels ocells
el-cant-dels-ocells.credit: Words: traditional Catalan, as printed by Lluís Millet (1917). Tune: traditional Catalan, as printed by Lluís Millet (1917). Arrangement: Lluís Millet (1867-1941), harmony printed 1917, adapted by Stackapella.

eliyahu-hanavi.title: Eliyahu HaNavi
eliyahu-hanavi.credit: Words: traditional Hebrew refrain. Tune: traditional Eastern Ashkenazi folk tune (as printed by A. Z. Idelsohn, 1929). Arrangement: Stackapella.

every-time-i-feel-the-spirit.title: Every Time I Feel the Spirit
every-time-i-feel-the-spirit.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (printed 1909). Tune: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (printed 1909). Arrangement: Stackapella.

ezekiel-saw-the-wheel.title: Ezekiel Saw the Wheel
ezekiel-saw-the-wheel.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (printed 1909). Tune: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (printed 1909). Arrangement: Stackapella.

go-down-moses.title: Go Down, Moses
go-down-moses.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, as sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers (published 1872). Tune: traditional spiritual, as sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers (published 1872). Arrangement: Stackapella, built on Theodore F. Seward's 1872 answer.

god-rest-ye.title: God Rest Ye Merry, Gentlemen
god-rest-ye.credit: Words: Traditional English (as printed by Bramley and Stainer, 1867). Tune: Traditional English (as printed by Bramley and Stainer, 1867). Arrangement: Bramley and Stainer's four parts (1867), adapted by Stackapella.

good-king-wenceslas.title: Good King Wenceslas
good-king-wenceslas.credit: Words: John Mason Neale (Carols for Christmas-tide, 1853). Tune: "Tempus adest floridum" (Piae Cantiones, 1582), as Thomas Helmore set it to Neale's words. Arrangement: Stackapella, on the chords of Bramley and Stainer's Christmas Carols New and Old.

greensleeves.title: Greensleeves
greensleeves.credit: Words: traditional (English, 16th century), as printed in William Chappell, Popular Music of the Olden Time (1855 to 1859). Tune: traditional (English, 16th century). Arrangement: Stackapella, on G. A. Macfarren's harmony (1855 to 1859).

happy-birthday.title: Happy Birthday
happy-birthday.credit: Words: Traditional (published 1911). Tune: "Good Morning to All", Mildred J. Hill (1893). Arrangement: Stackapella.

hark-the-herald.title: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
hark-the-herald.credit: Words: Charles Wesley (1739), altered by George Whitefield (1753) and others. Tune: Felix Mendelssohn (1840), adapted by William H. Cummings (1856). Arrangement: Hymns Ancient and Modern (1875), adapted by Stackapella.

haul-away-joe.title: Haul Away, Joe
haul-away-joe.credit: Words: traditional sea shanty (as sung by John Short, Watchet; printed 1914). Tune: traditional sea shanty (as sung by John Short, Watchet; printed 1914). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Cecil Sharp's harmony.

haul-on-the-bowline.title: Haul on the Bowline
haul-on-the-bowline.credit: Words: traditional sea shanty (as sung by John Short, Watchet; printed 1914). Tune: traditional sea shanty (as sung by John Short, Watchet; printed 1914). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Cecil Sharp's harmony.

heavenly-treasures.title: I Am Fill'd with Heavenly Treasures
heavenly-treasures.credit: Words: Shaker song (Mary Hazzard's songbook, about 1847). Tune: Shaker song (Mary Hazzard's songbook, about 1847). Arrangement: Stackapella.

hey-ho-nobody-home.title: Hey, Ho, Nobody Home (round)
hey-ho-nobody-home.credit: Words: anonymous (printed 1609). Tune: anonymous, in Thomas Ravenscroft's Pammelia (1609). Arrangement: Stackapella (round setting).

holy-holy-holy.title: Holy, Holy, Holy
holy-holy-holy.credit: Words: Reginald Heber (written by 1823). Tune: John Bacchus Dykes, "Nicaea" (1861). Arrangement: John Bacchus Dykes (1861), adapted by Stackapella.

home-on-the-range.title: Home on the Range
home-on-the-range.credit: Words: Brewster Higley (1872 or 1873). Tune: Daniel E. Kelley (1870s). Arrangement: Stackapella.

i-saw-three-ships.title: I Saw Three Ships
i-saw-three-ships.credit: Words: Traditional English (as printed by Bramley and Stainer). Tune: Traditional English, from Derbyshire (as printed by Bramley and Stainer). Arrangement: Stackapella, after John Stainer's harmony in Christmas Carols New and Old.

i-will-bow-and-be-simple.title: I Will Bow and Be Simple
i-will-bow-and-be-simple.credit: Words: Shaker song (Mary Hazzard's songbook, undated, between songs dated 1851 and 1852). Tune: Shaker song (Mary Hazzard's songbook, undated, between songs dated 1851 and 1852). Arrangement: Stackapella.

in-the-bleak-midwinter.title: In the Bleak Midwinter
in-the-bleak-midwinter.credit: Words: Christina G. Rossetti (1872). Tune: "Cranham", Gustav Holst (1906). Arrangement: Gustav Holst's four parts (The English Hymnal, 1906), adapted by Stackapella.

it-came-upon-the-midnight-clear.title: It Came Upon the Midnight Clear
it-came-upon-the-midnight-clear.credit: Words: Edmund Hamilton Sears (1849). Tune: "Carol", Richard Storrs Willis (1850, full form by 1869). Arrangement: Richard Storrs Willis's four parts (as printed by Charles L. Hutchins, 1916), adapted by Stackapella.

it-is-well.title: It Is Well with My Soul
it-is-well.credit: Words: Horatio G. Spafford (printed 1876). Tune: Philip P. Bliss, "Ville du Havre" (1876). Arrangement: Philip P. Bliss (1876), adapted by Stackapella.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.credit: Words: William Blake (c. 1804), from the preface to Milton. Tune: Hubert Parry, "Jerusalem" (1916). Arrangement: Parry's own accompaniment (1916), set for four voices by Stackapella.

jingle-bells.title: Jingle Bells
jingle-bells.credit: Words: James Lord Pierpont (1857). Tune: James Lord Pierpont (1857). Arrangement: Stackapella, on the 1909 printing's harmony.

joy-to-the-world.title: Joy to the World
joy-to-the-world.credit: Words: Isaac Watts (1719). Tune: "Antioch", arranged by Lowell Mason (1836). Arrangement: Lowell Mason's four parts (1848), adapted by Stackapella.

keep-on-the-sunny-side.title: Keep on the Sunny Side
keep-on-the-sunny-side.credit: Words: Ada Blenkhorn (1899). Tune: J. Howard Entwisle (1899). Arrangement: after J. Howard Entwisle's own four-part setting (1899), adapted for Stackapella.

ki-lo-naeh.title: Ki Lo Na'eh
ki-lo-naeh.credit: Words: traditional Hebrew hymn of the Passover Haggadah. Tune: traditional. Arrangement: Stackapella.

la-paloma.title: La Paloma
la-paloma.credit: Words: Sebastián Iradier, as usually credited (the 1859 Madrid edition names him for the music). Tune: Sebastián Iradier (published in Madrid, 1859). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Iradier's own chords.

las-mananitas.title: Las Mañanitas
las-mananitas.credit: Words: traditional Mexican. Tune: traditional Mexican. Arrangement: Stackapella.

leave-her-johnny.title: Leave Her, Johnny
leave-her-johnny.credit: Words: traditional sea shanty (John Short's version, as noted by Cecil Sharp, 1914). Tune: traditional sea shanty (John Short's version, as noted by Cecil Sharp, 1914). Arrangement: Stackapella.

lecha-dodi.title: Lecha Dodi
lecha-dodi.credit: Words: Solomon ha-Levi Alkabetz (16th century). Tune: traditional Ashkenazi melody for the Omer weeks (printed by Francis L. Cohen, 1904). Arrangement: Stackapella.

let-me-call-you-sweetheart.title: Let Me Call You Sweetheart
let-me-call-you-sweetheart.credit: Words: Beth Slater Whitson (1910). Tune: Leo Friedman (1910). Arrangement: Stackapella.

lift-every-voice.title: Lift Every Voice and Sing
lift-every-voice.credit: Words: James Weldon Johnson (1900). Tune: J. Rosamond Johnson (1900). Arrangement: J. Rosamond Johnson's own four parts (1900), adapted by Stackapella.

loch-lomond.title: Loch Lomond
loch-lomond.credit: Words: traditional Scottish. Tune: traditional Scottish. Arrangement: Stackapella.

londons-burning.title: London's Burning (round)
londons-burning.credit: Words: traditional; the line "Fetch the engines" is first found in Goss (1927), its maker unknown. Tune: traditional, as John Goss printed it in the Daily Express Community Song Book (1927). Arrangement: Stackapella (round setting).

maoz-tzur.title: Maoz Tzur
maoz-tzur.credit: Words: Hebrew piyyut signed Mordecai in its acrostic (12th or 13th century). Tune: traditional Ashkenazi Hanukkah tune (earliest known printing 1815; printed by Baer after 1883 and Idelsohn 1911/12). Arrangement: Stackapella, on A. Z. Idelsohn's harmony (1911/12).

michael-row.title: Michael, Row the Boat Ashore
michael-row.credit: Words: traditional spiritual (Slave Songs of the United States, 1867). Tune: traditional spiritual (1867). Arrangement: Stackapella.

nearer-my-god.title: Nearer, My God, to Thee
nearer-my-god.credit: Words: Sarah Flower Adams (1841). Tune: Lowell Mason, "Bethany" (usually dated 1856). Arrangement: Lowell Mason's four parts (1859), adapted by Stackapella.

noche-de-paz.title: Noche de paz
noche-de-paz.credit: Words: Spanish words after Joseph Mohr's German (1816), as printed, unsigned, in El Himnario evangélico (New York, 1893); often credited to Federico Fliedner (in 13 of the 18 hymnals from 1990 on that Hymnary.org indexes), though no printing we have seen before 1964 names him. Tune: Franz Xaver Gruber (1818). Arrangement: Stackapella.

now-is-the-month-of-maying.title: Now Is the Month of Maying
now-is-the-month-of-maying.credit: Words: anonymous (printed 1595). Tune: Thomas Morley (1595). Arrangement: Thomas Morley (1595), his five voices as four for Stackapella.

now-thank-we-all-our-god.title: Now Thank We All Our God
now-thank-we-all-our-god.credit: Words: Martin Rinkart, "Nun danket alle Gott", translated by Catherine Winkworth (Lyra Germanica, second series, 1858). Tune: Johann Crüger, "Nun danket". Arrangement: Felix Mendelssohn's harmony as The Hymnal (1916) prints it, adapted by Stackapella.

o-come-all-ye-faithful.title: O Come, All Ye Faithful
o-come-all-ye-faithful.credit: Words: Latin hymn "Adeste Fideles" (18th century); English words Frederick Oakeley (1841), as revised in Murray's Hymnal (1852). Tune: "Adeste Fideles", attributed to John Francis Wade (c. 1743). Arrangement: Stackapella.

o-come-o-come-emmanuel.title: O Come, O Come, Emmanuel
o-come-o-come-emmanuel.credit: Words: John Mason Neale (1851), as altered for Hymns Ancient and Modern (1861). Tune: "Veni Emmanuel", from the Hymnal Noted (musical editor Thomas Helmore). Arrangement: W. H. Monk's four parts (1861), adapted by Stackapella.

o-holy-night.title: O Holy Night
o-holy-night.credit: Words: Placide Cappeau (French, 1847); English words John Sullivan Dwight (1855). Tune: Adolphe Adam (1847). Arrangement: Refrain as printed in Carols Old and Carols New (1916); verse set for four voices by Stackapella on its organ harmony.

o-little-town-of-bethlehem.title: O Little Town of Bethlehem
o-little-town-of-bethlehem.credit: Words: Phillips Brooks (1868). Tune: Lewis H. Redner, "St. Louis" (1868). Arrangement: Lewis H. Redner's four parts as Carols Old and Carols New (1916) prints them, adapted by Stackapella.

o-the-beautiful-treasure.title: O the Beautiful Treasure
o-the-beautiful-treasure.credit: Words: Shaker song (Mary Hazzard's songbook, about 1849). Tune: Shaker song (Mary Hazzard's songbook, about 1849). Arrangement: Stackapella.

ode-to-joy.title: Ode to Joy (Joyful, Joyful)
ode-to-joy.credit: Words: Henry van Dyke (published 1911). Tune: Ludwig van Beethoven, Symphony No. 9 (1824). Arrangement: Stackapella.

oh-how-lovely.title: Oh, How Lovely Is the Evening (round)
oh-how-lovely.credit: Words: English words anonymous (printed 1896), after the German round "O wie wohl ist mir am Abend". Tune: German round (O wie wohl ist mir am Abend), a folk round after a canon by Karl Friedrich Schulz (died 1850). Arrangement: Stackapella (round setting).

oy-chanukah.title: Oy Chanukah
oy-chanukah.credit: Words: Mordkhe Rivesman (printed 1911/12). Tune: traditional Hasidic tune (printed 1911/12). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Pesach Lvov's arrangement (1911/12).

oyfn-pripetchik.title: Oyfn Pripetchik
oyfn-pripetchik.credit: Words: Mark Warshawsky (printed 1901). Tune: Mark Warshawsky (printed 1911/12). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Pesach Lvov's arrangement (1911/12).

pastores-a-belen.title: Pastores a Belén
pastores-a-belen.credit: Words: unsigned, as printed in Cánticos espirituales con música (Las Vegas, New Mexico, 1916). Tune: unsigned, as printed in Cánticos espirituales con música (Las Vegas, New Mexico, 1916). Arrangement: Stackapella.

praise-to-the-lord.title: Praise to the Lord, the Almighty
praise-to-the-lord.credit: Words: Joachim Neander (1680), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1863). Tune: German chorale "Lobe den Herren" (earliest known printing: Stralsund Gesangbuch, 1665). Arrangement: William Sterndale Bennett and Otto Goldschmidt (1863), adapted by Stackapella.

red-red-rose.title: My Love Is Like a Red, Red Rose
red-red-rose.credit: Words: Robert Burns (1794). Tune: traditional Scottish, "Low down in the Broom", as printed by R. A. Smith. Arrangement: Stackapella.

riu-riu-chiu.title: Riu, Riu, Chiu
riu-riu-chiu.credit: Words: anonymous, from Villancicos de diversos autores (Venice, 1556). Tune: anonymous, from Villancicos de diversos autores (Venice, 1556); attributed by some to Mateo Flecha the Elder or Bartomeu Càrceres. Arrangement: the 1556 print's own four voices, adapted by Stackapella.

row-row-row.title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat (round)
row-row-row.credit: Words: traditional (in print by 1881). Tune: traditional, The Franklin Square Song Collection (1881), credited to Eliphalet Oram Lyte. Arrangement: Stackapella.

rozhinkes-mit-mandlen.title: Rozhinkes mit Mandlen
rozhinkes-mit-mandlen.credit: Words: Abraham Goldfaden. Tune: Abraham Goldfaden. Arrangement: Stackapella.

sakura-sakura.title: Sakura Sakura
sakura-sakura.credit: Words: traditional Japanese. Tune: traditional Japanese (printed 1888). Arrangement: Stackapella, held notes in the koto's manner.

shall-we-gather.title: Shall We Gather at the River
shall-we-gather.credit: Words: Robert Lowry (1864). Tune: Robert Lowry (1864). Arrangement: Robert Lowry's four parts (1869), adapted by Stackapella.

shchedryk.title: Shchedryk
shchedryk.credit: Words: traditional Ukrainian shchedrivka (New Year song). Tune: traditional Ukrainian folk melody. Arrangement: Stackapella.

shenandoah.title: Shenandoah
shenandoah.credit: Words: traditional American (19th century). Tune: traditional, as printed by Richard Runciman Terry in The Shanty Book, Part I (1921). Arrangement: Stackapella.

shorty-george-blues.title: Shorty George Blues
shorty-george-blues.credit: Words: George W. Thomas and Hociel Thomas (1924). Tune: George W. Thomas (1924). Arrangement: Stackapella.

shoshanat-yaakov.title: Shoshanat Yaakov
shoshanat-yaakov.credit: Words: traditional Hebrew Purim hymn. Tune: synagogue tune, as Abraham Baer printed it (after 1883). Arrangement: Stackapella.

silent-night.title: Silent Night
silent-night.credit: Words: Joseph Mohr (1816); English words John Freeman Young (1859). Tune: Franz Xaver Gruber (1818). Arrangement: Stackapella.

simple-gifts.title: Simple Gifts
simple-gifts.credit: Words: Joseph Brackett (attributed; usually dated 1848). Tune: Joseph Brackett (attributed; usually dated 1848). Arrangement: Stackapella.

skye-boat-song.title: The Skye Boat Song
skye-boat-song.credit: Words: Harold Boulton (Songs of the North, printed by 1888). Tune: Hebridean boatmen's air, four bars added by Anne Campbell Macleod (Songs of the North). Arrangement: Malcolm Lawson (Songs of the North), adapted by Stackapella.

spanish-ladies.title: Spanish Ladies
spanish-ladies.credit: Words: traditional sea shanty (as sung by Captain Lewis, Minehead; printed 1909). Tune: traditional sea shanty (as sung by Captain Lewis, Minehead; printed 1909). Arrangement: Stackapella, on Cecil Sharp's harmony.

steal-away.title: Steal Away
steal-away.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, attributed to Wallace Willis (published 1872). Tune: traditional spiritual (published 1872). Arrangement: Stackapella.

sweet-adeline.title: Sweet Adeline
sweet-adeline.credit: Words: Richard H. Gerard (1903). Tune: Harry Armstrong (1903). Arrangement: Stackapella.

swing-low.title: Swing Low, Sweet Chariot
swing-low.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, attributed to Wallace Willis (published 1872). Tune: traditional spiritual (published 1872). Arrangement: Stackapella.

the-first-noel.title: The First Noel
the-first-noel.credit: Words: Traditional English (as printed by Bramley and Stainer, 1867). Tune: Traditional English (as printed by Bramley and Stainer, 1867). Arrangement: John Stainer's four parts, adapted by Stackapella.

the-holly-and-the-ivy.title: The Holly and the Ivy
the-holly-and-the-ivy.credit: Words: Traditional English (as printed by Cecil Sharp, 1911). Tune: Traditional English, as sung by Mrs Mary Clayton of Chipping Campden (noted and printed by Cecil Sharp, 1911). Arrangement: Stackapella.

the-lord-bless-you.title: The Lord Bless You and Keep You
the-lord-bless-you.credit: Words: Numbers 6:24 to 26 (King James Version), as Lutkin set them. Tune: Peter C. Lutkin (1900). Arrangement: Lutkin's four parts (1900), adapted by Stackapella.

the-water-is-wide.title: The Water Is Wide
the-water-is-wide.credit: Words: traditional, as collected by Cecil Sharp and Charles Marson, Folk Songs from Somerset, third series (1906), no. 66, verses 1 and 6. Tune: traditional, sung by Mrs Cox of High Ham, collected by Cecil Sharp (1906). Arrangement: Stackapella.

three-blind-mice.title: Three Blind Mice (round)
three-blind-mice.credit: Words: traditional. Tune: traditional, as printed in Home Songs (Oliver Ditson, 1906). Arrangement: Stackapella (round setting).

tzur-mishelo.title: Tzur Mishelo
tzur-mishelo.credit: Words: traditional Hebrew Sabbath table hymn (zemer), anonymous. Tune: German melody for the Sabbath zemirot (printed by Francis L. Cohen, 1906). Arrangement: Stackapella.

wade-in-the-water.title: Wade in the Water
wade-in-the-water.credit: Words: traditional spiritual (printed 1904). Tune: traditional spiritual (printed 1904). Arrangement: Stackapella.

we-gather-together.title: We Gather Together
we-gather-together.credit: Words: Theodore Baker (1894), from the Dutch "Wilt heden nu treden" in Adrianus Valerius's Nederlandtsche Gedenck-clanck (1626). Tune: "Kremser", a Netherlands folk tune printed by Valerius (1626), as Eduard Kremser arranged it. Arrangement: The four parts for the tune Kremser as The Beacon Hymnal printed them (1924), adapted by Stackapella.

we-three-kings.title: We Three Kings of Orient Are
we-three-kings.credit: Words: John Henry Hopkins Jr. (1857). Tune: John Henry Hopkins Jr. (1857). Arrangement: John Henry Hopkins Jr.'s trio and chorus (1863?), adapted by Stackapella.

were-you-there.title: Were You There
were-you-there.credit: Words: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (published 1909). Tune: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (published 1909). Arrangement: Stackapella.

what-child-is-this.title: What Child Is This?
what-child-is-this.credit: Words: William Chatterton Dix (as printed in Bramley and Stainer, Christmas Carols New and Old). Tune: Greensleeves, Old English (as printed in Bramley and Stainer, Christmas Carols New and Old). Arrangement: Stackapella, on the harmony of Bramley and Stainer's Christmas Carols New and Old.

white-coral-bells.title: White Coral Bells (round)
white-coral-bells.credit: Words: anonymous (printed 1916). Tune: anonymous, printed as "May Bells" in Hollis Dann's Fourth Year Music (1916). Arrangement: Stackapella (round setting).

who-will-bow-and-bend.title: Who Will Bow and Bend
who-will-bow-and-bend.credit: Words: Shaker song (Mary Hazzard's songbook, about 1847). Tune: Shaker song (Mary Hazzard's songbook, about 1847). Arrangement: Stackapella.

will-ye-no-come-back-again.title: Will Ye No Come Back Again?
will-ye-no-come-back-again.credit: Words: Carolina Oliphant, Lady Nairne (1766 to 1845). Tune: as printed under Finlay Dun's name (1795 to 1853). Arrangement: Stackapella.

with-cat-like-tread.title: With Cat-like Tread
with-cat-like-tread.credit: Words: W. S. Gilbert (1879). Tune: Arthur Sullivan (1879). Arrangement: Arthur Sullivan (1879), adapted by Stackapella.

ye-banks-and-braes.title: Ye Banks and Braes o' Bonnie Doon
ye-banks-and-braes.credit: Words: Robert Burns (printed 1792). Tune: "The Caledonian Hunt's Delight", by James Miller, fashioned into a tune by Stephen Clarke (printed 1792; sung here as G. F. Graham printed it in 1849). Arrangement: Stackapella.
